ai.definition: Green Ammonia, Iron-Air Batteries, Nuclear Waste Transmutation, and Space-Based Solar Power are advanced technologies aimed at addressing the challenges of renewable energy storage, generation, and waste management.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technologies are in the early stages of development, with some pilot projects but no widespread commercial implementation yet.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at this stage, dependent on technological advancements, regulatory support, and market acceptance.

glossary.def: A clean energy carrier produced from renewable electricity, hydrogen, and nitrogen for use in various industrial applications.
An electrochemical storage device that uses iron anodes and atmospheric oxygen to generate electrical energy with long cycle life.
A process where radioactive isotopes in spent nuclear fuel are converted into less hazardous elements through nuclear reactions.
A concept of capturing and transmitting solar energy from satellites orbiting Earth to terrestrial receivers for use on the ground.
